nodes.name: Invoice
nodes.annotation_note: The only entity within the declared canonical boundary (silver_reconciliation_standard). One row represents one invoice line, on either the vendor-statement side or the internal-ERP side, distinguished by record_source (see A-003/SV-001). Excluded-candidate rationale for every other F01-inventoried table is recorded in this file's synthesis summary, not per-node, since none of them meet the promotion bar within this boundary.

nodes.name: id
nodes.business_meaning: Internal row identifier, no business meaning.

nodes.name: record_id
nodes.business_meaning: Stable, reproducible identifier for this line, derived from source+invoice+amount — the closest thing to a natural key.

nodes.name: record_source
nodes.business_meaning: Which side of the reconciliation this row represents.

nodes.name: document_type
nodes.business_meaning: NOT_DETERMINABLE

nodes.name: statement_id
nodes.business_meaning: Groups all lines belonging to one reconciliation run/statement.

nodes.name: statement_date
nodes.business_meaning: NOT_DETERMINABLE
nodes.disambiguation_note: Despite the name, this column does not store a real statement date on the VENDOR_STATEMENT side — normalize_to_silver() (notebooks/01_document_intake.py) writes the row's statement_period string into it as a stand-in ('statement_date — use period as proxy', per its own inline comment). A field genuinely named for a date holds a period value instead. See the ANNOTATION_CHECKLIST item raised from this finding.

nodes.name: vendor_id
nodes.business_meaning: Vendor identifier.
nodes.disambiguation_note: Not an independently assigned ID — deterministically derived from vendor_name (upper-cased, underscored) at write time. See F02 Naming Pattern Flags.

nodes.name: vendor_name
nodes.business_meaning: Vendor display name, either AI-extracted or filename-derived as a fallback.

nodes.name: shop
nodes.business_meaning: The paying shop/location, when the vendor statement identifies one.

nodes.name: invoice_number
nodes.business_meaning: The vendor's invoice identifier — the primary business key the matching engine keys off.
nodes.disambiguation_note: Application-layer invariant (INV-04, docs/INVARIANTS.md) requires this to never be null in practice — not database-enforced (see F01 Constraint Inventory). Stored exactly as extracted, no normalization (RULE-01) — see A-011 for the separate normalized copy.

nodes.name: invoice_number_normalized
nodes.business_meaning: Computed solely for matching comparison — the original (A-010) is always retained separately and is what gets stored on a match/exception record.

nodes.name: invoice_date
nodes.business_meaning: Date the invoice was issued.

nodes.name: ro_number
nodes.business_meaning: Repair order reference — the Level 2 matching key when invoice_number alone doesn't match.

nodes.name: po_number
nodes.business_meaning: Purchase order reference.

nodes.name: work_order_number
nodes.business_meaning: Work order reference.

nodes.name: amount
nodes.business_meaning: The original charge amount.
nodes.disambiguation_note: On vendors whose statement layout has only one amount column, this and outstanding_amount (A-018) are set to the same value by explicit fallback logic (validate_invoice()) — see F02 Naming Pattern Flags.

nodes.name: credit
nodes.business_meaning: Credit/payment amount applied against the invoice, when the vendor's layout reports one.

nodes.name: outstanding_amount
nodes.business_meaning: What's still owed — the amount the matching engine actually compares.
nodes.disambiguation_note: See A-016 — can be a fallback copy of amount, not independently sourced, on single-amount-column vendors. Application-layer invariant (INV-04) requires this to never be null in practice.

nodes.name: due_date
nodes.business_meaning: Payment due date.

nodes.name: posting_date
nodes.business_meaning: ERP posting date.
nodes.disambiguation_note: Explicitly set to null on the VENDOR_STATEMENT side — an ERP-only concept, confirmed by an inline code comment ('ERP concept, not applicable here') at the exact write site.

nodes.name: status
nodes.business_meaning: ERP posting status (see SV/SVV note below — this field is NOT part of the promoted vocabulary; its values live on the excluded bronze_internal_erp_raw/gold side, not observed as populated on the VENDOR_STATEMENT side of this same table).
nodes.disambiguation_note: One of seven distinctly-scoped '*status'-shaped fields across this schema — see F02 Naming Pattern Flags. Explicitly null on the VENDOR_STATEMENT side (same code comment as A-020) — an ERP-only concept.

nodes.name: description
nodes.business_meaning: Free-text line description, when the vendor's layout provides one.

nodes.name: currency
nodes.business_meaning: Currency code — USD assumed throughout the current codebase.

nodes.name: statement_period
nodes.business_meaning: The YYYY-MM billing period this line belongs to.

nodes.name: source_file
nodes.business_meaning: Originating PDF filename — technical provenance, not itself a business fact about the invoice.

nodes.name: ingestion_timestamp
nodes.business_meaning: When this row was written — technical provenance.
This line came from the vendor's own PDF statement.
This line was generated as the internal/ERP-side counterpart (mock ERP today; a real NetSuite export in future).

cross_graph_edges.note: Writes the VENDOR_STATEMENT side via normalize_to_silver().
Writes the INTERNAL_ERP side via normalize_erp_to_silver().
Matching engine reads both record_source sides to classify matches — not an owner/writer of this entity.

excluded_candidates.rationale: Bronze pipeline internal — raw, untyped AI output, not a domain entity (BCE-005 exclusion of pipeline internals).

Derived match OUTCOME of the Invoice entity, not the entity itself. Structurally entity-like (could be modeled as a 'Match' entity in a richer domain model) but outside the declared canonical boundary (Silver only) — excluded per boundary, not for lack of business meaning. Worth revisiting if the canonical_layer_boundary declaration is ever widened.
Same reasoning as gold_matched_invoices — a genuine 'Exception' business concept, excluded solely by boundary scope.
A derived per-run snapshot ('Reconciliation Run' concept), excluded by boundary scope.
Platform/audit metadata table, not a domain entity.
A genuine 'Disposition' business concept (the human decision record), excluded by boundary scope — same category as gold_exceptions.
Platform identity table, not a reconciliation-domain entity.
